doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: The conversational Mance trio, duo music and violinist Michi
summary: Mance wants players interacting rather than taking turns; the trio developed duo-style intimacy and sometimes adds a violinist.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Actually this trio is kind of different. And Junior really wanted to play talking together sometimes. Not this is a piano solo. Not this is a bass solo. But he wanted to play sometimes all together. Sometimes speak all together. You know he plays something, even if this is his solo, but I play something — that’s why he made this trio. So he said this was the first experience of this kind. It’s just happened after he started hiring me and we kind of developed a duo, just a duo, minus the drums, just a duo. Duo music is different from trio music. So he kind of started an intimate way of creating music. And his student, Michi, anyway, always sometime he wanted to use a violin player. And mostly classical training. The violin player cannot play in any key sometimes. But she is more flexible. So that’s the history of how that happened.
